title: Google Extends Voluntary Exit Offers to Staff in Five More Countries as AI Costs Rise
excerpt: Reuters reports Google confirmed it began offering voluntary exit packages in June to some employees in Canada, France, Germany, Japan and Switzerland, while keeping its AI and cloud units out of the programme.
body:
• Google has expanded its voluntary exit programme this year to some employees in Canada, France, Germany, Japan and Switzerland, Reuters reported on Wednesday, as Alphabet reins in costs while spending heavily on artificial intelligence.
  • In Switzerland, where terms were reported, staff who accepted received one month salary for each year of service, capped at 12 months; employees were told in mid-June, given decisions by mid-July, and departures began in August.
  • Google Cloud and the AI unit DeepMind have been excluded from the buyout offers; chief financial officer Anat Ashkenazi has repeatedly named AI and cloud as the company hiring priorities.
  • Reuters could not determine how many employees accepted the latest offers, and Google has not disclosed the numbers — so the scale of this round is not yet known.

Google cost-cutting has gone properly global. Alphabet Google confirmed to Reuters that it began offering voluntary exit packages in June to some employees in Canada, France, Germany, Japan and Switzerland — an expansion, first reported on Wednesday, of a programme that since last year had run in some divisions in the United States and Britain.

"In 2025, some of our teams introduced a voluntary exit program with severance. This past summer, in June, we expanded this program globally in a few countries to support our important work ahead."

— Google spokesperson, in a statement to Reuters

What the Swiss terms show

Switzerland is the only country for which Reuters obtained the terms. Google employs about 5,000 people there, around a major engineering hub in Zurich, and three people familiar with the matter said the programme covered multiple divisions but excluded DeepMind, the AI research unit. Staff were told about the packages in mid-June and given responses by mid-July if they applied; those who accepted received one month salary for each year of service, up to a maximum of 12 months, and departures began in August. Terms and eligibility in the other four countries have not been reported, and neither Google nor Reuters has put a number on how many employees were offered packages or took them.

https://www.instagram.com/p/Deh2M9uki1P/

The pattern: everything is cut except AI

The exclusions describe the strategy. Employees in Google Cloud and DeepMind have been kept out of past buyout offers, and chief financial officer Anat Ashkenazi has repeatedly highlighted AI and cloud computing as the company key hiring priorities in earnings presentations, Reuters noted. The offers come as mounting AI spending has unnerved Wall Street and dented Alphabet stock price. Google is not the only one: Microsoft last week offered voluntary buyouts to 60,000 employees in an effort to contain costs. The industry shape is consistent — headcount and cost discipline in the legacy business, protected hiring in the AI core.

Storyboard18 reported the same expansion, noting the programme was extended to a limited number of countries in June to support the company future priorities. What would change the picture is a number: until Google discloses acceptances or a savings target, this round is a direction of travel, not a measurable restructuring.
